convention: The same three-state convention as messages/lg.needs-translation.json, for the Delivery namespace: a key is translated, awaiting a translator, or identical on purpose. Every key under needsTranslation below holds the ENGLISH text verbatim, because the agent that wrote this namespace does not speak Luganda. Two kinds of string here are why a guess was not made anyway: the sentences that describe what a rider is and is not told, which are a data-protection disclosure a patient consents on the strength of, and the sentence about refunds, which names who owes the money. Getting either subtly wrong in Luganda would be a misrepresentation, not a typo. src/i18n/i18n.test.ts checks only the BASE catalogues, so nothing enforces this file; it is a worklist for a translator, not a gate.
translateFirst: Delivery.riderKnowsNothing, Delivery.deliveryNeedsConsent and Delivery.contentsNote first — they are the disclosure the patient is agreeing to when they choose delivery, and a patient who cannot read them is consenting to something they were not told. Then Delivery.controlledBody (a legal refusal with no override, which has to be understood the first time) and Delivery.refundHonesty (who actually holds the money). The status.* words are next: they are what somebody waiting for a package reads over and over, and they are short enough to translate confidently.

translated.Delivery.medicinesLabel: Eddagala — the ordinary Luganda word for medicine. Short, unambiguous, and used for the same thing on the Prescriptions screen.
